# @favy/di

> @favy/di v3 builds TypeScript 5+ dependency graphs from typed, named functions without decorators or container configuration.

The standard `Module` is lazy and run-cached; `Live<T>` carries transitive requirements; the API Reference is authoritative for public signatures and types.

## Core documentation

- [Introduction](https://di.favy.dev/guides/introduction/): Learn the core concepts and build a first dependency graph.
- [Module](https://di.favy.dev/module/module/): Understand named providers, dependency maps, and composition.
- [API Reference](https://di.favy.dev/reference/api/): Consult the authoritative public signatures and types.
- [Partial Application](https://di.favy.dev/module/partial/): Bind known dependencies with `.provide()` while preserving the remaining types.
- [Caching](https://di.favy.dev/module/cache/): Compare run, module, and uncached lifecycles.
- [Lazy Initialization](https://di.favy.dev/module/lazy/): See when providers resolve and which operations trigger them.

## Guides

- [Testing](https://di.favy.dev/guides/testing/): Replace dependencies at the composition root for deterministic tests.
- [Best Practices](https://di.favy.dev/guides/best-practices/): Apply recommended patterns for clear, maintainable graphs.

## Optional

- [Transform Input](https://di.favy.dev/module/transform-input/): Customize dependency inputs, including HKT-based transforms.
- [Transform Output](https://di.favy.dev/module/transform-output/): Customize callable outputs, including HKT-based transforms.
- [Source Repository](https://github.com/favyorg/di): Inspect the implementation, report issues, and contribute.
